name: whosthere-edd8d439-blind30-ots
instr:
# whosthere gives wrong answers everywhere — diagnosing it without a test suite

A command-line tool that finds the machines answering on the local link and lists them for you now gets almost everything it does wrong, and the mistakes look unrelated to each other. Nothing about the local link changed and nothing about the way the tool is invoked changed. The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything that could be observed from the outside, in the order the problems were hit.

Telling it how to behave fails before anything is looked for. Asking where the program keeps its preferences on disk answers wrongly: with the environment variable that names the user preference folder aimed at a temporary place, the answer is a home-relative default rather than something beneath that place, and with that same variable removed from the environment the answer is again not the home-relative default. The folder used for things kept between runs is wrong the other way round, since with nothing set in the environment the query comes back with no folder at all rather than the default beneath the home folder. Reading those preferences misbehaves too. A time value written as a plain number, such as 15 or a padded 30, is refused with an error instead of being taken as that many seconds.
